preamble: Gliding of the alveolar implosive under palatalization: [ɗ] becomes [j]. Gravina (2014) calls the change *ɗ > j "very widespread" in Central Chadic. It applies to words carrying the reconstructed palatalization prosody, so the change is more precisely *ɗʲ > j: the palatalized implosive loses its closure and leaves only the palatal glide. It is especially frequent word-finally, where many groups have -aj for Proto-Central Chadic *-ɨɗʸ.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Central Chadic to Mofu, Sukur, Musgum and Hurza

sources: Gravina, R. (2014). The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: The Reconstruction of the Phonology and Lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the Linguistic History of the Central Chadic Languages. PhD dissertation, Leiden University (LOT). https://hdl.handle.net/1887/30139
